source: Recorded 2026-10-10 from codex-acp 2.1.1 by a direct ACP client advertising AIR v1 sessionFailure, asyncTasks and nativeSubagentSessions. codexNativeTurn: two parallel subagents, one launching a nested subagent, a permission request from a subagent (answered allow once), and a steer injected while they ran. codexNativeCancelled: one subagent, then session/cancel on the parent. codexNativeReplay: session/load of the same session in a new adapter process. Paths are rewritten to /work/repo, /tmp/claude and /Users/me, the local user name to me, the machine's hostname to host.local wherever it appears (in streamed text too, where it spans chunks), quota metadata is removed, and auth status and available-command frames are left out; nothing else is edited. Follow-ups, recorded 2026-10-10 from the same adapter in another session: codexNativeFirstRun runs one subagent; codexNativeResumed is the next turn, where the parent messages that finished subagent; codexNativeRunningFollowUp launches another and messages it while it runs. In each turn the parent's first frame is moved to the front; nothing else is reordered. A terminal's output frames beyond 50 keep the first and last two (9996 removed: the sandboxed ping's repeated recvmsg errors).

update.title: Use two subagents in parallel. Subagent A: list the files in this directory, then launch its own nested subagent that reads README.md and replies with a one-sentence summary; A reports that summary. Subagent B: create a file named notes.txt containing the single line hello, using your file editing tool. When both finish, tell me in two sentences what they did.

content.text: Use two subagents in parallel. Subagent A: list the files in this directory, then launch its own nested subagent that reads README.md and replies with a one-sentence summary; A reports that summary. Subagent B: create a file named notes.txt containing the single line hello, using your file editing tool. When both finish, tell me in two sentences what they did.
I’ll launch both subagents in parallel and report their results in two sentences when they finish.
README.md describes a tiny demo project used to record subagent sessions.
Directory listing: `.git/` and `README.md`. My nested subagent read README.md and summarized it: “README.md describes a tiny demo project used to record subagent sessions.”
Created notes.txt using apply_patch and verified that it contains the single line `hello`.
Also, at the end, tell me the current year.

Subagent A listed `.git/` and `README.md`, then its nested subagent summarized README.md as describing a tiny demo project used to record subagent sessions. Subagent B created `notes.txt` containing the single line `hello`; the current year is 2026.
Use one subagent: it should run the shell command `sleep 60 && echo done` and then report the output.
I’ll have one subagent run the command and report its output.

update.title: Use one subagent (a general-purpose agent, so it can be resumed) to read README.md and report its first line. Wait for it, then tell me what it said.
